Report: Savvy Games Group CEO Brian Ward departs company
'As Savvy embarks on its next period of transformational growth, this is the right time for new leadership for that evolution.'
Bryant Francis
,
Senior Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
September 1, 2026
2 Min Read
Image via Savvy Games Group
Saudi Arabian video game conglomerate Savvy Games Group appears to be experiencing a change in leadership. That's according to a report from
Bloomberg News
, which states that CEO Brian Ward is stepping down from his position.
Ward apparently announced the news to Savvy employees in a message stating that it is "the right time for new leadership" as it "embarks on its next period of transformational growth." He is apparently being temporarily replaced by Turqi Alnowaiser, deputy governor of Savvy Game Group's parent organization: the government-owned Saudi Arabia Public Investment fund (PIF). Alnowaiser also is the head of the PIF's international investments division.
Ward became CEO of Savvy Games Group in 2021 and oversaw
a $37.8 billion
spree of international investments and acquisitions in game companies large and small. During his time as CEO, Savvy acquired significant stakes in companies like
Embracer Group
,
Take-Two Entertainment
, and
Nintendo
. Its most significant acquisitions include its $4.9 billion purchase of mobile developer
Scopely
and its $3.5 billion acquisition of
Pokémon Go
developer
Niantic
.

As those investments progressed, industry professionals
expressed growing concern
about the PIF's ownership of Savvy, which links the conglomerate to the Saudi government. Those concerns were
echoed by members of the US Congress
after the PIF led
a joint $55 billion buyout
of Battlefield and The Sims developer Electronic Arts (EA) that did not directly involve Savvy itself.
However, the buyout of EA may be driving difficult questions inside Savvy Games Group. Sources speaking to Bloomberg say the purchase of EA has raised concern over "how the two giant Saudi-owned video-game businesses will be run."
It isn't clear if this concern played any role in Ward's departure.
